# Preface {.unnumbered}

This tutorial grew from a real workflow-portability exercise on the DLDCC HPC
cluster at Baylor College of Medicine. The useful parts were not only the
successful commands. The difficult parts—an incompatible Java garbage
collector, a full home-directory quota, a broken package solve, container PATH
differences and non-identical BAM headers—exposed the engineering ideas that a
beginner most needs to understand.

The book therefore preserves failures as teaching material. An error message
is not evidence that you are unsuited to computational work. It is an
observation about a system. The goal is to learn how to turn that observation
into a small, testable hypothesis.

## Companion project

The commands and evidence are grounded in version `v0.1.0` of the
[NGS Workflow Portability Lab](https://github.com/cjgunase/ngs-workflow-portability-lab/tree/v0.1.0).
Linking the book to a tagged release prevents the underlying example from
silently changing while someone is following the tutorial.

## A note about HPC systems

Cluster names, module names, partitions, accounts and storage paths are local
policy. DLDCC-specific commands are labeled as examples. Readers should ask
their own administrators for the equivalent settings rather than copying site
configuration blindly.
